name: Prologue
speaker: grandpa
desc: You wake up in the scrapyard. Grandpa is tinkering with a broken generator nearby. Another day in the Scrapyard District.

name: Getting Organized
speaker: grandpa
desc: Grandpa nods approvingly at your new sorting station. 'Your father used to keep things organized too,' he says, looking away.

name: The Workshop Awakens
speaker: grandpa
desc: As the workshop powers up for the first time in years, you notice scratches on the workbench — measurements, notes, a name: your father's.

name: Father's Legacy
speaker: grandpa
desc: Behind the rusted door, covered in dust and cobwebs, stands a mecha. Small, old, battered — but unmistakably your father's first build. The cockpit still has his callsign etched into the frame.

name: Turning Junk Into Future
speaker: grandpa
desc: The refinery hums to life. Grandpa watches from the doorway. 'He always said this machine would change everything,' he whispers. 'He wasn't wrong.'

name: First Schematic
speaker: system
desc: You study the Nano Infra schematics. The engineering is elegant — far beyond what you'd expect from street tech. Where did these come from?

name: The Bazaar
speaker: system
desc: The Neon Bazaar is everything they warned you about — and more. Holographic vendors, whispered deals, and the unmistakable scent of opportunity.

name: The Empty Workshop
speaker: system
desc: The workshop is quieter now. The tools are where he left them. The bench he built forty years ago still stands against the wall. Some things outlast the people who made them.

name: Routines
speaker: system
desc: The sorting station runs. The refinery hums. The scrapyard does what it was built to do. You keep working. It's what he would have wanted.

name: Father's Debt
speaker: ironjaw_enforcer
desc: The enforcer drops a dataslate on the workbench without a word. The number is not small. 'Your old man borrowed from us. You're his blood. You figure it out.' He walks out. The door doesn't close all the way.

choices.label: Pay what you can
choices.desc: Buy time. Compliance now, options later.
choices.log: You hand over what you have. The clock keeps ticking.

choices.label: Refuse — it's not your debt
choices.desc: Stand your ground. Escalation is likely.
choices.log: You close the door they left open. The Ironjaw won't forget.

name: The Covenant Extends a Hand
speaker: covenant_liaison
desc: A message arrives through an Underground contact. No sender. Just a frequency and a time window. 'We've observed your operational profile. The Steel Covenant has infrastructure. You have potential. This arrangement benefits both parties.' Someone with resources is paying attention.

choices.label: Hear them out
choices.desc: Information is leverage. Learn what they want.
choices.log: You acknowledge the contact. The Covenant notes your response.

choices.label: Refuse contact
choices.desc: Keep distance. Some hands you don't shake.
choices.log: You drop the frequency. Autonomy maintained — for now.

name: Something in the Pile
speaker: system
desc: While sorting a deep pile of electronic scrap, you find something unusual — a humanoid frame, half-buried in circuit boards. It's small. Industrial design. Old but not broken. One eye flickers with residual power.

choices.label: Bring it to the workshop and power it up
choices.desc: It's in rough shape, but the workshop has what you need.
choices.log: It boots. One eye flickers open. 'TASK... ASSIGN... TASK...'

choices.label: Study it first, then repair carefully
choices.desc: Rushing repairs on unknown tech is how you lose fingers.
choices.log: 'Kinetic Industrial Task Automaton, designation K.I.T.A. Ready for assignment.'

choices.label: Strip it for components
choices.desc: An intact android frame is worth more as parts than as a helper.
choices.log: The android is dismantled. Grandpa watches from the doorway in silence.

name: Nephilim in the Yard
speaker: kenji
desc: They weren't just salvaging. I've seen scan patterns like that before — systematic, targeted. Someone hired them to look for something specific. Something in this yard. Something they already know exists. We need to figure out what before they come back with more.

name: Moving Up the Ranks
desc: Lieutenant Reyes calls you in. 'You've got instincts. I can push your promotion through — but there's a condition. We've got a suspect in holding. Probably guilty. But probably isn't enough for a warrant. You want to move up or not?'

choices.label: Wait for a proper warrant
choices.log: Reyes nods slowly. 'I respect that. Promotion approved — the slow way.' You move up clean.

choices.label: Sign the papers
choices.log: Reyes slides the papers across. 'Welcome to the next rung. Try not to think about it too hard.'

name: The Taeyang File
desc: A junior officer hands you a drive. 'Someone left this. Taeyang Corp financials — routed through precinct accounts.' Your superior is in the building. This could end careers. Including yours.

choices.label: Report it to Internal Affairs
choices.log: You make the call. By morning, three officers are on leave. Reyes looks at you differently now. So does the city.

choices.label: Destroy the drive
choices.log: The drive goes in the furnace. Two days later, an envelope arrives. No return address. Full of creds.

name: The Supplier's Offer
desc: A supplier offers you a side arrangement: take overstock off their hands at half price, sell it at full to the refugee camp upriver. 'They need it. You profit. Everyone wins.' Except you'd be the one setting the price.

choices.label: Sell it at cost — just cover the transport
choices.log: Word spreads. The camp remembers. A few weeks later, three new regular customers show up at your stand. The supplier seems confused but doesn't complain.

choices.label: Sell at full market rate — they're not your problem
choices.log: You profit. The camp pays. You don't lose any sleep over it. You tell yourself this is correct. Mostly you believe it.

name: The Taeyang Supply Contract
desc: Taeyang Corp needs a distribution partner for a new product line. The contract is worth more than your current year's income. The product: behavioral modification hardware, labeled as 'therapeutic wellness devices.'

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.log: Taeyang marks you 'uncooperative.' Your other clients notice you turned down the big contract. Some respect it. One increases their order.

choices.label: Take the contract — business is business
choices.log: The creds clear. The product ships. You don't open the crates. You decide not to ask what's in them.

name: The Corporate Leak
desc: You've found something during a routine security audit: a trove of Taeyang Corp internal communications. Nothing illegal in having them. Very illegal in how they were obtained. A journalist will pay well. So will Taeyang.

choices.label: Send it to the district's independent feed
choices.log: The story runs for three days. Taeyang issues a denial. The denial is less convincing than the data. You don't collect much money. You collect something else.

choices.label: Sell it back to Taeyang — let them bury it
choices.log: Taeyang pays promptly. The story never runs. A contact sends you one message: 'I know it was you.' They don't elaborate. They don't have to.

name: The Recruitment
desc: A message arrives through channels that shouldn't exist. 'We know what you can do. We have resources you don't. The alternative is we make your current clients aware of your methods.' Taeyang's digital warfare division is recruiting.

choices.label: Refuse — and start covering your tracks
choices.log: You spend three days rebuilding your anonymity architecture. It costs time and creds. When you're done, the silence from Taeyang is either acceptance or a longer game. You decide it doesn't matter.

choices.label: Accept — the resources are real
choices.log: The first briefing arrives. The work is clean — for now. You tell yourself you'll know when to walk away. You've said that before.

name: The Dive
desc: An intermediary approaches after training. 'Next match — we need you to lose in round two. Not badly. Believably. The syndicate has money on your opponent.' The number they quote is real money.

choices.label: Fight clean — no dive
choices.log: You win. The crowd goes louder than expected. The intermediary doesn't approach you again. You're told the syndicate had a backup plan. You don't ask what it was.

choices.label: Take the money — lose the fight
choices.log: You go down in round two. Convincing. The crowd boos. The money arrives. You tell yourself it's one fight. It's always just one fight.

name: The Corporate Ringer
desc: The next ranked opponent is a Taeyang-sponsored fighter with corporate-grade hardware. Your handler pulls you aside: 'There's a buyout on the table. Walk away from the championship circuit, take the payout, let them own the rank.' The number is generous.

choices.label: Get in the ring — win or die trying
choices.log: The fight runs long. The crowd is silent for most of it. You win on points, barely. Taeyang withdraws their fighter. The circuit is yours — for now.

choices.label: Take the payout — the number is real
choices.log: You sign the agreement. The rank goes to the ringer by default. You have money and no title. Hayashi doesn't call for two weeks.
